lean_mathlib_joint_statement.who: "Lean and Mathlib communities"; the page says the statement is endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative; no individual is named
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.says: quoted: "We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" and "We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct"; the four criteria of Kevin Buzzard's post of 2026-11-12 (xenaproject.wordpress.com) are said to be satisfied
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.statement: Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, which the page says "has been carefully vetted by experts in Lean and number theory"
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.compilation: "dozens of people have reported correct compilation of the codebase, reproducing the same raw proof export file"
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.statement_match: a community file isolates the statement and imports only Mathlib; compared with the proved theorem by two tools, comparator and con-leche --compare, "both confirming" it is exactly Mathlib's statement
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.proof_validity: the exported proof checked by Lean's kernel, con-leche, con-ron and several third-party checkers in different languages; con-leche and con-ron described as carrying a formal proof, relative to set theory, that they cannot accept a false proof; checks ran on an inert export
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.scope: the statement concerns the Riemann Hypothesis only; it does not mention the four Dirichlet L-function statements
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.on_the_mathematics: one sentence: "We look forward to all the activity in the mathematical community that will help explain the new ideas in this proof."
lean_mathlib_joint_statement.words: the page uses the word certify; in this record that word is a standing reached under the rule in prereg_cycle1.yaml A1, which this statement does not address, so it is recorded as what the page says and moves nothing by itself
